classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the common perpendicular height, calculate two triangle areas and find their difference.

inlines.text: A farmer uses fencing to divide a triangular piece of land into two smaller triangles, as shown.
What is the difference in the two areas?

spec.description: Triangle with horizontal top edge, vertical left edge and a right-angle marker at the upper-left vertex. A red dashed fence runs from the lower-left vertex to the top edge. The top segments are labelled 18 m and 26 m; the common perpendicular height is labelled 40 m.
spec.mathematics: Both smaller triangles have perpendicular height 40 m, with bases 18 m and 26 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the dividing fence are visible; calculated areas and their difference are answer-only.

answer.worked:
Both triangles have perpendicular height $40\,\mathrm{m}$.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{left}} &= \frac{18\times40}{2}\\
A_{\text{left}} &= 360\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
A_{\text{right}} &= \frac{26\times40}{2}\\
A_{\text{right}} &= 520\,\mathrm{m}^2\\
\text{Difference} &= 520-360\\
\text{Difference} &= 160\,\mathrm{m}^2
\end{align*}$$
